title: Card Relationship Reductions to the Per-Item Overdraft Charge on Personal Checking
content:
**Clause.** The charge applied to each chargeable overdraft item on a Personal Checking account is reduced where the owner's record under Personal Credit Cards, or a premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts, reaches the levels below.

- Where the owner has made at least 10 card payments in the last twelve months **and** at least 4 overdraft charges stand on the account, each chargeable item is charged at the tier's overdraft fee for each item less a deep relationship reduction of 4.25.
- Where the case above does not apply **and** either the owner has made at least 4 card payments in the last twelve months **or** the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, each chargeable item is charged at the tier's overdraft fee for each item less a relationship reduction of 2.5.
- Where neither case applies, no such reduction is made.

The tier's overdraft fee for each item is the figure the tier publishes:

| Tier | Charge for each item paid into overdraft (USD) |
|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 |
| Student Checking | 15.00 |
| Everyday Checking | 35.00 |
| Interest Checking | 35.00 |
| Premier Checking | 35.00 |
| Private Client Checking | 0.00 |

**Worked reductions on hypothetical inputs.** On a tier charging 35.00 for each item, an owner with 12 card payments in the last twelve months and 5 overdraft charges standing meets the first case, and each chargeable item is charged at 35.00 less 4.25, which is 30.75. An owner with 5 card payments and 2 charges standing meets only the second case, and each chargeable item is charged at 35.00 less 2.5, which is 32.50. An owner with 2 card payments and no premier money market balance meets neither, and the reduction does not arise.

The first case requires both of its limbs; the second is met by either limb alone. Equality satisfies each threshold, so exactly 10 card payments with exactly 4 charges standing reaches the first case.
